summary: Extends JSpecify diamond-operator nullability handling to anonymous classes, recovering the instantiated supertype from assignment, return, and parameter contexts so override checks in the anonymous body use it.

tests.evidence: Feature/bug fix mandates tests; after rebase the initial approach caused a stack overflow with no covering test (commits 'Fix stackoverflow', 'Add regression test for stackoverflow'), and CodeRabbit asked for a generic-method-with-concrete-parameter case; a test comment was later found out of date and the test renamed.

user_docs.evidence: No option or docs page; behavior of existing JSpecify mode extends to a new construct.

doc_comments.evidence: CodeRabbit asked for Javadoc on isCallNeedingInference; the final version documents the new getConstructedTypeAtCallSite; minor.

change_description.evidence: Description links the issue and lists the contexts; includes AI disclosure; fine.

performance.evidence: Adds context lookups on the inference path; the stack overflow was a recursion defect, not a cost issue.

backward_compat.evidence: Previously skipped anonymous diamond classes now get checked, so users may see new errors under JSpecify mode; expected for this mode.

error_model.evidence: Diagnostics for overrides in anonymous diamond bodies change (GenericsTests expectations adjusted).

correctness.evidence: Initial design mixed anonymous-class handling into inference; msridhar pointed out the body does not influence diamond inference, the approach produced a stack overflow and a false positive, and the final fix was rewritten around getConstructedTypeAtCallSite using the class identifier.

user_value.evidence: Closes a requested issue (#1475); worth it, API unchanged.

surprising_behavior.evidence: New warnings on anonymous diamond bodies; strict-supertype cases kept conservative to avoid false positives.

contradictions.evidence: Removes obsolete TODOs; one test comment left stale in the reviewed version (msridhar: 'this comment is out of date').

spec_conformance.evidence: Interprets JLS diamond inference for anonymous classes (JLS 15.9.3) and JSpecify; reviewer noted the initial structure treated anonymous diamond inference differently from plain diamond calls, contrary to the language rule.

plan.why: One file of logic plus tests; the required axes all hinge on the same inference reasoning, so one reviewer covers them best.
